qualification: Proved on TP1's in-memory ledger (the job authority's statements included) with generated test_only tables. No database, object store, dispatcher loop or served HTTP walk was run.
defect: The table-profile/1 payload did not state the size of the original it reads, so G22S's workbookScratchMiB reserves the 8 GiB maximum for every workbook read.
decisions: D1 table-profile-worker.ts: TableProfileInputSchema gains an optional top-level sourceBytes (positive safe integer). queueTableProfileTx sets it to Number(row.bytes) from the source row tableFromOriginal already loaded under its row lock, before the payload is fingerprinted, so it is part of input_fingerprint and usp_job_metadata.input_sha256.
D1 the job id stays stableUuid('table-profile/1:<sourceId>:<sourceRevision>:<requestKey>'); it never hashed the payload, so it is unchanged.

D1 a payload queued before TPB has no sourceBytes; the strict schema parses it without adding the key, so its fingerprint, registerUspJobInputTx's scope check and the accept-time payload comparison are unchanged and the job runs; the dispatcher reserves the largest workbook's scratch for it, as before.
D2 the worker's read, the request path, the public contract and the dispatcher are unchanged.
